title: Grade 9 Mathematics — Quadrilaterals
description: Properties of quadrilaterals — parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezium
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The sum of all angles in a quadrilateral is:
questions.explanation: The angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360°. Any quadrilateral can be divided into 2 triangles, each with 180°, giving 2 × 180° = 360°.

questions.question: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are:
questions.explanation: Parallelogram properties: (1) opposite sides are equal and parallel, (2) opposite angles are equal, (3) diagonals bisect each other, (4) consecutive angles are supplementary.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rectangle are:
options: Equal and bisect each other at right angles
Equal and bisect each other (but NOT necessarily at right angles)
Equal but do not bisect each other
questions.explanation: Rectangle: diagonals are EQUAL in length and bisect each other. They do NOT intersect at right angles (that property belongs to rhombus and square). All angles = 90°.

questions.question: A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other at right angles but are NOT equal is a:
questions.explanation: Rhombus: all sides equal, diagonals bisect each other at 90° but are NOT equal. Rectangle: equal diagonals but not at 90°. Square: equal diagonals AND at 90°.

questions.question: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. Find ∠B.
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, consecutive angles are supplementary: ∠A + ∠B = 180°. ∠B = 180° − 70° = 110°.

questions.question: The Midpoint Theorem states that the line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is:
options: Half the length of the third side and parallel to it
questions.explanation: Midpoint Theorem: The line joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length. This is a key theorem for quadrilateral proofs.

questions.question: A trapezium has:
options: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel
Exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel
questions.explanation: A trapezium (UK) / trapezoid (US) has exactly ONE pair of parallel sides (called the parallel sides or bases). A parallelogram has TWO pairs of parallel sides.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a square?
options: Diagonals bisect each other at right angles
questions.explanation: In a square: all sides equal, all angles 90°, diagonals are EQUAL AND bisect each other at 90°. 'Unequal diagonals' is NOT a property of a square — it is a property of a rhombus (non-square).

questions.question: In parallelogram PQRS, diagonals PR and QS bisect at O. If PO = 5 cm, find PR.
questions.explanation: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. If PO = 5 cm (half of PR), then PR = 2 × PO = 10 cm.

questions.question: A parallelogram is a rectangle if and only if:
options: Its diagonals are equal in length
It has at least one right angle
questions.explanation: A parallelogram is a rectangle if and only if its diagonals are equal (in length). Equal diagonals in a parallelogram mean all angles are 90°.

questions.question: In a rhombus ABCD, ∠ABC = 60°. Find ∠ADC.
questions.explanation: In a rhombus (also a parallelogram), opposite angles are equal. ∠ABC = ∠ADC = 60°. Adjacent angles are supplementary: ∠BAD = ∠BCD = 120°.

questions.question: The area of a parallelogram is:
questions.explanation: Area of parallelogram = base × height (perpendicular height). Area of rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ (product of diagonals). Area of triangle = ½ × base × height.

questions.question: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are parallelograms. Therefore:
questions.explanation: If square → rectangle → parallelogram (by the given statements), then by transitivity: all squares are parallelograms. The reverse implications are not valid (not all parallelograms are rectangles).

questions.question: A kite has:
options: Both pairs of opposite sides equal
Two pairs of adjacent sides equal
questions.explanation: A kite has two pairs of ADJACENT (neighbouring) sides equal: e.g., AB=AD and CB=CD. It has one pair of equal opposite angles and diagonals that are perpendicular.

questions.question: ABCD is a parallelogram. If AB = 2x − 3 and CD = x + 4, find x.
questions.explanation: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal: AB = CD. 2x − 3 = x + 4 → x = 7. Then AB = CD = 11.
